title: Thin-capping layer epitaxial quantum dots for near-field quantum photonics
authors: Yuting Guo, Jonathan Bar-David, Pasquale Cilibrizzi, Sung-Yul L. Park, Jin Dong Song, Luca Sapienza
abstract: Epitaxial quantum dots (QDs) are widely recognised as one of the best quantum light sources, given their good stability, brightness, quantum efficiency and coherence. To reach such properties, QDs are protected from potentially detrimental surface states by a relatively thick capping layer, typically exceeding 50nm. This prevents the implementation of near-field effects, like plasmonic-based ones, that can dramatically increase the light-matter interaction, since the control of the spontaneous emission dynamics and directionality of the emission can only occur if the emitter is in close proximity (typically tens of nanometers or less) from the metallic structures. In this work, we report the growth and optical characterisation of InAs/GaAs QDs with GaAs capping layer thickness of 10nm, 20nm, and a more standard 95nm. Remarkably, we observe emission linewidths up to 5 times smaller than previously reported, with unperturbed excitonic lifetimes. These results demonstrate that the epitaxial QD's high optical quality can be maintained even when the emitters are at reduced distances from the surface, opening the path for the exploration of near-field light-matter interactions with coherent and stable emitters, suitable for quantum technology applications.
summary: This paper reports on the growth and optical characterization of InAs/GaAs quantum dots capped with very thin layers. The key finding is that these QDs maintain excellent optical quality, including narrow linewidths and long lifetimes, even when placed close to the surface. This breakthrough opens a viable path for utilizing these stable emitters in near-field quantum photonic applications.
main_problem: The challenge is to enable near-field quantum photonics applications by bringing quantum emitters close to metallic structures while maintaining the high optical quality of the quantum dots.
main_result: The study demonstrates that InAs/GaAs quantum dots maintain high optical quality, exhibiting significantly narrow emission linewidths and stable excitonic lifetimes even when capped with very thin GaAs layers (10-20 nm).
method: The research involved growing InAs/GaAs QDs using MBE with varying GaAs capping layer thicknesses (10 nm, 20 nm, 95 nm) and characterizing them using micro-photoluminescence, time-resolved PL, and spectroscopy.
model_or_system: The physical system is InAs/GaAs epitaxial quantum dots. The experiment varies the thickness of the GaAs capping layer (CL) to control the proximity of the emitter to the surface, which is critical for near-field light-matter interactions.
key_observables: Emission linewidths (observed up to 5 times smaller than previous reports), excitonic lifetimes ($\sim 0.9-1.1$ ns), and PL spectra evolution.
important_parameters: GaAs capping layer thickness (10 nm, 20 nm, 95 nm); near-field separation (tens of nanometers or less).
main_assumptions: The good optical quality in thin-capped structures suggests that detrimental surface effects are mitigated in these specific QDs, allowing for near-field coupling.
figures_summary: Figures show PL spectra evolution with power, linewidth/intensity vs. power density, and time-resolved PL measurements confirming stable lifetimes across different capping layer thicknesses.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for near-field coupling, presents the experimental growth and characterization of QDs with varying thin capping layers, and reports measurements showing preserved optical quality despite reduced separation from the surface.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics as it experimentally validates a pathway to integrate stable quantum emitters into plasmonic/near-field photonic devices, a key goal in quantum technology.
